statement: Across New York City's 42 UHF neighbourhoods, asthma emergency department visit rates are higher where NYCCAS annual average NO2 and PM2.5 are higher, and the association survives adjustment for neighbourhood poverty.

graph_evidence.summary: 91 ratio findings; 78 above 1, 12 below; 59 with CI above 1, 7 with CI below 1; median ratio 1.16 (mixed increments and designs)
157 ratio findings; 144 above 1, 9 below; 88 with CI above 1, 4 with CI below 1; median ratio 1.15 (mixed increments and designs)
140 ratio findings; 131 above 1, 7 below; 85 with CI above 1, 1 with CI below 1; median ratio 1.2 (mixed increments and designs)

graph_evidence.note: Abstracts read on PubMed: 24858282 (NJ pediatric ED, PM2.5 RR per IQR 1.03, 1.02-1.04); 33254941 (California, NO2 per 5 ppb lag 0-30 OR 1.56, 1.43-1.70); 16984840 (Taichung, ecological Pearson r = 0.72 NO2 vs child ED visits, one year).

literature.citation: Zheng X-y et al. (2015). Association between air pollutants and asthma emergency room visits and hospital admissions in time series studies: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS ONE 10(9):e0138146.
literature.finding: Pooled short-term RR: PM2.5 1.023 (1.015-1.031); NO2 1.018 (1.014-1.022) (increment as reported in the paper, read as per 10 ug/m3).

literature.citation: Khreis H et al. (2017). Exposure to traffic-related air pollution and risk of development of childhood asthma. Environ Int 100:1-31.
literature.finding: Asthma development: NO2 RR 1.05 (1.02-1.07) per 4 ug/m3; PM2.5 1.03 (1.01-1.05) per 1 ug/m3.

prediction.magnitude: Unadjusted: rate ratio of asthma ED visits per 10 ppb NO2 between 1.3 and 3 (far above the long-term research value of about 1.05 per 4 ug/m3, i.e. about 1.25 per 10 ppb), because the neighbourhood gradient carries poverty, housing and access to care. Poverty-adjusted: the NO2 ratio shrinks by more than half and its interval may include 1. PM2.5: weaker than NO2 and possibly null or negative, because PM2.5 is highest in midtown Manhattan.
prediction.support_if: Poverty-adjusted NO2 rate ratio > 1 with a 95% interval above 1.
prediction.refute_if: Poverty-adjusted NO2 rate ratio <= 1 with an interval that excludes the research value.

plan: Data: NYC DOHMH Environment and Health Data Portal (github.com/nychealth/EHDP-data, commit hash recorded) and NYC Open Data c3uy-2p5r (Air Quality, NYCCAS annual averages by UHF42). Outcome: asthma ED visit rate per 10,000 by UHF42, children 5-17 if available, else all ages; the most recent years available before 2020 (average of up to three years) to avoid the COVID disruption, with the same years of NYCCAS annual NO2 and PM2.5. Covariate: percent of residents below the federal poverty level (EHDP, UHF42). Do NOT use the EHDP 'PM2.5-attributable asthma ED visits' indicator, which is derived from research concentration-response functions and would be circular. Model: OLS of log rate on pollutant (per 10 ppb NO2; per 1 ug/m3 PM2.5), then adding poverty; HC3 standard errors; sensitivity with borough fixed effects and with both pollutants. Figure: scatter of UHF neighbourhoods (log rate vs NO2) coloured by poverty, with the research slope drawn through the city mean.
alternatives: Poverty and the conditions that travel with it (housing quality, pests, mould, smoking, access to primary care)
Ecological fallacy: residence of ED patients vs where exposure occurs; UHF averages hide within-area variation
Spatial autocorrelation: the Bronx cluster drives the fit (borough FE sensitivity)
Diagnosis and ED-use practices that vary with insurance
